mascot.pet.guide.board.hello: This is the board~ Hot, Today and Weekly are in the row up top.
mascot.pet.guide.board.q1: What's the difference between Today and Hot?
mascot.pet.guide.board.a1: Today only counts cards listed in the last 24 hours. Hot ranks every card on the site, with the most-chatted ones first.
mascot.pet.guide.board.q2: How do I see just one genre?
mascot.pet.guide.board.a2: Just tap a genre tag. You can pick several. Genres you don't want to see can be hidden in settings.
mascot.pet.guide.board.q3: Can I jump to a card if I know its number?
mascot.pet.guide.board.a3: Yep! Type the card number in the search box and press Enter to jump right to it.
mascot.pet.guide.search.hello: What are you looking for? You can search character names, source titles and tags~
mascot.pet.guide.search.a1: Try the source title or a tag instead. Source titles work in Traditional or Simplified Chinese, and short names work too.
mascot.pet.guide.search.q2: Can I see just one source?
mascot.pet.guide.search.a2: Yep, there's a source filter above the results.
mascot.pet.guide.editor.hello: Writing a card? Tap me if anything's unclear~
mascot.pet.guide.editor.q1: What do I have to fill in?
mascot.pet.guide.editor.a1: Three things: name, persona and opening message. Any section on the left with a red dot is still missing something.
mascot.pet.guide.editor.q2: How do I get on the board?
mascot.pet.guide.editor.a2: Hit Publish, answer the rating questions and confirm the source, and it goes to review. Once it passes, it's on the board. There's a weekly listing quota.
mascot.pet.guide.editor.a3: Yep, the test chat panel on the side lets you chat with your card right away.
mascot.pet.guide.card.hello: This is the card page. Hit "Start chat" to play~
mascot.pet.guide.card.a1: It goes into your Library so you can find it in one tap. The author also gets to know someone likes it.
mascot.pet.guide.card.a2: They're everyone's ratings. A card with only a few votes won't shoot to the top from a single one.
mascot.pet.guide.card.a3: If the author has tips turned on, there's a tip button on this page. Comments and favorites count as support too!
mascot.pet.guide.author.hello: This is the author's page. Follow them and you'll get notified about new cards.
mascot.pet.guide.author.a1: When they post or update a card, the bell lets you know. You'll get it through push notifications or Discord DMs too if you've turned those on.
mascot.pet.guide.library.hello: Everything you've chatted with, favorited and followed is here.
mascot.pet.guide.library.a1: Chats save automatically. Hit "Continue chat" here to pick up where you left off.
mascot.pet.guide.library.q2: What's the difference between favorites and follows?
mascot.pet.guide.library.a2: You favorite cards and follow authors.
mascot.pet.guide.mine.hello: All your cards are here, and you can check their review status too.
mascot.pet.guide.mine.q1: How many cards can I list each week?
mascot.pet.guide.mine.a1: This week's listing quota is shown up top and resets every Monday. If you run out, you can use extra listing packs.
mascot.pet.guide.mine.q2: What if my card got rejected?
mascot.pet.guide.mine.a2: The reason is written on the card. Fix it up and submit again.
mascot.pet.guide.mine.q3: Editing a card that's already listed?
mascot.pet.guide.mine.a3: If you change the name, summary, cover, tags or opening message, it goes back to review.
mascot.pet.guide.wallet.hello: These are your credits. Chatting uses them.
mascot.pet.guide.wallet.a1: Credits with an expiry date. Once they expire, they're gone. You can see every entry in the history below.
mascot.pet.guide.wallet.a2: Hit Top up and you'll pay in the HarperHarbor console. Come back after paying and the credits will be there.
mascot.pet.guide.referral.hello: Invite your friends and you'll both get credits.
mascot.pet.guide.referral.a1: Send your friend your invite code or link. It counts once they sign up and enter it.
mascot.pet.guide.referral.q2: A friend gave me an invite code?
mascot.pet.guide.referral.a2: Enter it under "Enter invite code". There's a time limit, so do it within a few days of signing up.
mascot.pet.guide.badges.a1: Each badge shows its requirements and your progress. Playing cards, writing cards, favoriting and commenting all count.
mascot.pet.guide.badges.q2: Can I show off just a few?
mascot.pet.guide.badges.a2: You can pick a few as featured, or make the whole wall private.
mascot.pet.guide.community.hello: Link your Discord and I'll recognize you over there too!
mascot.pet.guide.community.a1: Chatting on Discord earns you XP and levels. I can also DM you notifications.
mascot.pet.guide.community.q2: How do I report a problem?
mascot.pet.guide.community.a2: You can open a report here, and support will follow up with you on Discord.
mascot.pet.guide.notifications.hello: Who replied to you and what your followed authors posted, it's all here.
mascot.pet.guide.notifications.q1: Want alerts even when you're off the site?
mascot.pet.guide.notifications.a1: Turn on browser push notifications, or link Discord so I can DM you.
mascot.pet.guide.notifications.a2: You can turn off on-site notifications or like notifications up top.
mascot.pet.guide.me.hello: This is your profile page. Your info and all kinds of shortcuts are here.
mascot.pet.guide.me.q1: How do I change my nickname and avatar?
mascot.pet.guide.me.a1: Just edit your profile on this page.
mascot.pet.guide.settings.hello: Set up your player persona here, plus what kind of content you want to see.
mascot.pet.guide.settings.a1: It decides what the characters in a card call you and who they think you are.
mascot.pet.guide.settings.q2: Don't want to see some genres?
mascot.pet.guide.settings.a2: Check them and they'll be hidden from the board and search. You can undo it anytime.
mascot.pet.guide.resources.hello: This is your asset library. Put any images for your cards here.
mascot.pet.guide.resources.q1: Anything to watch out for when renaming files?
mascot.pet.guide.resources.a1: Renaming a file or moving it to another folder changes its link, so update any cards that use it!
mascot.pet.guide.guide.hello: The card-writing guide~ It covers writing with an AI assistant and with the web editor.
mascot.pet.guide.guide.a1: An AI assistant is fastest. Just describe the character you want clearly. If you'd rather fine-tune it yourself, use the web editor.
mascot.pet.guide.developers.hello: Developer docs. Check here if you want to integrate or manage cards with code.
mascot.pet.guide.developers.a1: There's a command-line tool. Once an AI assistant sets it up, it can write and upload cards for you.
mascot.pet.guide.updates.hello: Everything that's changed on the site lately is here~
mascot.pet.guide.download.hello: Want Hearthroom on your phone? Look here.
mascot.pet.guide.download.q1: How do I install it on iPhone?
mascot.pet.guide.download.a1: Open the site in Safari, tap Share, then choose "Add to Home Screen".
mascot.pet.guide.review.q1: What if I claim a card and don't get to it?
mascot.pet.guide.review.a1: If you don't act on it for a while after claiming, it goes back to the queue for someone else.
mascot.pet.guide.review.a2: Put it back in the queue and let another reviewer take a look. No need to force a call.

editor.lede.new: Fill this in and it's ready to talk. Already have a Tavern card? Drop it in and the fields fill themselves.
editor.world.lede: World mode: this card is a world with several characters. The world itself is the character definition under Persona, and the world-level lore is the Lorebook bound to this card; only the characters live here. Each turn the world first decides what happened and who is present, then up to a few characters answer in their own voice, each knowing only what they saw or were told.
editor.world.experimental: World mode is still experimental and may not behave as expected, so use it for testing and trying things out, and keep it off cards you plan to publish.
editor.world.disable: Turn world mode off (characters are removed when you save)
editor.world.maxSpeakers: Characters who may speak per turn
editor.world.strictness: How far the world honours what the player declares
editor.world.strictness.lenient: Lenient: what the player says happens
editor.world.strictness.balanced: Balanced: ordinary outcomes as stated; anything involving others or hidden facts is decided by the world
editor.world.strictness.strict: Strict: the player only states intent; the world decides every outcome
editor.world.char.name: Name
editor.world.char.id.hint: Lowercase letters, digits, underscore or hyphen; leave empty to derive it from the name. Do not change it after saving: past messages and pending events refer to it.
editor.world.char.profile.hint: One or two sentences the world and the other characters all know.
editor.world.char.description: Full definition (seen only by this character)
editor.world.char.description.hint: Can be long. It enters only this character's own context; the world and the other characters never see it.
editor.world.char.lorebook.hint: Same as the card's Lorebook: create one, import a file, or pick one you already have. It is recalled only when this character speaks; the other characters and the world never see it.
editor.name: Character name
editor.nickname.hint: {'{{char}}'} in the definition becomes this; leave empty to use the character name.
editor.creator: Original author credit
editor.creator.placeholder: Filled in automatically for imported cards
editor.creator.hint: Credit and version are only written into exported cards; not shown on the site.
editor.language.hint: The language decides which board this card appears on. After creation, only Traditional and Simplified Chinese can be swapped.
editor.language.scriptHint: Players whose interface uses the same script see your text as written, and the rest see it converted, so pick the script the card is actually written in.
editor.detail.hint: The heart of the card: who they are, how they speak, what situation they're in. The more concrete, the more consistent the replies.
editor.contract.hint: What a reply should look like: how many paragraphs, whether to narrate, how to mark actions. Leave empty for the default.
editor.jailbreak.hint: Appended to every turn. Put the one or two rules that get forgotten most.
editor.welcome.hint: The first thing a player reads. Set the scene and the relationship here, or the story never starts.
editor.alternates.hint: A different way in, same story. Before the first message, players can swipe between them and pick one; the main opening is the default.
editor.prologue.hint: First lines the player can just tap. Much better than staring at an empty box.
editor.talkExample.hint: A few exchanges showing how this character talks. Two or three is plenty; more locks them in.
editor.background.hint: Portrait, 9:16. Also used for the chat avatar and exported image. Keep important details inside the dashed safe zone.
editor.backgroundLandscape.hint: Used on wide screens, 16:9. If empty, the portrait background is cropped instead.
editor.shareImage.hint: The large preview when a link is posted to Discord, LINE or X. 1200×630, keep the title and main character in the middle. If empty, the landscape background is used, then the portrait background.
editor.blockers: {n} more item(s) upstream; you'll see them when you submit.
editor.publish.hint: Your card appears in the community after HearthRoom approves it.
editor.publish.saveFirst: You have unsaved changes. Save once before submitting.
editor.publish.confirm: This card goes into review, and becomes visible to everyone once it passes. Submit?
editor.publicNotice: This card is public. Saving will switch it back to private first; submit it for review again when you are done. Anyone who already has the link can keep playing.
editor.reviewNotice: This card is under review. You can edit it once the review is finished.
editor.delete.hint: Removes the card along with its chats, lorebook bindings, and board listing. This cannot be undone.
editor.delete.confirmMessage: The card and all of its chats will be gone for good.
editor.needName: Give this card a name first.
wb.lede: A lorebook holds what doesn't belong in every turn but has to be right when it comes up: places, terms, side characters. It's pulled in when a keyword is mentioned.
wb.empty: This card has no lorebook yet.
wb.name: Lorebook name
wb.entry.name: Entry name
wb.entry.keywords.placeholder: Comma separated, e.g. Rain City, Old Docks
wb.entry.keywords.hint: Mention any one of these and this entry joins the conversation.
wb.entry.keywords.constantHint: Set to always-on, so it's included every turn regardless of keywords.
wb.entry.deleteConfirm: Deleting this entry can't be undone. Sure?
import.formats: PNG, JSON and CHARX character cards are supported
import.review.title: Read: {name}
import.review.overwrite: Applying this replaces what's currently in the form.
import.dropped.title: These didn't come across
import.drop.position: Insertion position on {n} entries. Where lore goes is decided here.
import.drop.caseSensitive: Case sensitivity on {n} entries. Matching here is always case-insensitive.
import.drop.bookSettings: Lorebook scan depth and budget. Handled here by the conversation's memory budget.
import.drop.mesExample: Example dialogue: the format didn't say who said what, so nothing was split out. You can add it under Dialogue.
import.note.groupGreetings: {n} group-chat-only greetings were merged into the alternate greetings. There is no group chat here, but they still work as openings.
import.drop.decorators: Decorators in {n} lorebook entries ({names}). The site decides where and how often entries are inserted; always-on, disabled and extra keywords were honoured.
import.drop.assets: {n} bundled assets (expression sprites, sounds and the like). Only the main portrait and main background are kept.
import.error.invalid: That file isn't a character card, or it's damaged.
import.error.noMetadata: No character data in that PNG — it's just an image.
import.mmd.drop: Drop the three MMD export files here, all at once or one by one
import.mmd.formats: Regex export (JSON), worldbook (JSON), character definition (TXT). Any subset applies; fill the rest in the form.
import.mmd.error.invalidJson: {name}: broken JSON, could not read it.
import.mmd.error.unknown: {name}: doesn't look like a regex, worldbook, or definition file.
import.mmd.detailTooLong: The definition is {n} characters, over this site's limit of {max}. Trim it after applying before you can save.
export.title: Export
export.hint: Save it in the common format and take it elsewhere.
export.pngFallback: PNG export failed, so a JSON file containing the card settings was downloaded instead.
state.uploadFailed: Upload failed. Try another image or again later.
editor.draftRestored: Restored the draft you didn't save last time.
import.landed.image: 1 embedded illustration, used as the portrait background
import.avatarFailed: The portrait couldn't be uploaded. Pick an image again under Images.
import.drop.tags: {n} extra tag(s). A card here holds at most 10, so only the first 10 were kept.
wb.import.error: No lorebook entries in this file. Use a lorebook JSON exported from SillyTavern, or a card that carries one.
wb.import.done: Imported {n} entries. The whole book now matches the file once you save.
wb.entry.secondary.placeholder: Leave empty to trigger on keywords alone
wb.entry.secondary.hint: When set, both must appear: any keyword plus any of these.
import.split.entries: {n} entries were longer than {max} characters and were split into parts sharing the same keywords; nothing was cut.
editor.worldbook.entryTooLong: Worldbook entry "{name}" is over {max} characters and can't be saved. Split it into two entries with the same keywords for the same effect.
wb.entry.content.over: Over {max} characters won't be accepted; split it into two entries with the same keywords for the same effect.
regex.title: Regex rules
regex.bar.hint: AI replies are rewritten by these rules on the player's screen before they show.
regex.pick: Pick a rule on the left, or add one.
regex.rule.name: Name
regex.rule.find.placeholder: /『([\s\S]*?)』/g or a literal marker such as <status>
regex.rule.find.literal: Literal text: every occurrence is replaced.
regex.rule.replace.hint: HTML, CSS and JS are allowed.
regex.statusbar.hint: A fixed block on the top layer of the chat page. Viewers see it, the AI never does. Put markers for global styling and side tools here; rules expand them too.
regex.lowered.hint: When checked it sits under the composer.
regex.test.placeholder: Paste an AI reply to preview the result
regex.discard: Changes haven't been applied to the form. Close anyway?
regex.imported: Read {n} rules. They save with the card.

download.title: Download Hearthroom
download.intro: Keep the role-card community on your phone. Come back to find characters and write stories.
download.requirement: Android 8.0 or later · Internet connection required
download.step1: Download the APK on your Android phone, then open the file.
download.step2: If prompted, allow this browser to install apps.
download.step3: Tap Install. Once installed, open Hearthroom from your home screen.
download.updates: When an app update is available, you can read what changed before downloading it and confirming installation. Website features update with the site, without reinstalling the app.
download.browserIntro: Open Hearthroom in your browser. You can also add it to your home screen or install it as a web app.
download.ios: iPhone / iPad: open this site in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
download.desktop: Desktop: choose Install Hearthroom from the menu or address bar of a supported browser. If that option is unavailable, use the website directly.
download.bannerBody: Install the app and return to the community from your home screen.
authorization.notice: Hearthroom encrypts and saves the provider authorization you approve so you can use it after signing in on another device.
authorization.storage: Hearthroom stores your linked provider identity and encrypted access and refresh credentials. Encryption keys are managed separately from the database. Your provider password is never received.
authorization.access: The backend renews credentials within the permissions you grant. The browser and player hold short-lived access credentials in memory. Administrators with backend execution access can still decrypt stored credentials; this storage is not risk-free.
authorization.control: You can stop authorization here or revoke it on the provider’s authorized apps page. Active credentials are removed after revocation; encrypted credentials are retained for retry if revocation fails. Account links and community records remain.
authorization.migration: Your first sign-in through this flow requires authorization again. Old browser-only credentials are cleared rather than uploaded automatically.
authorization.disconnectConfirm: Stopping authorization for {provider} affects all devices. You must authorize it again to use this service. Your community account and records remain.
authorization.pending: Hearthroom has stopped using this authorization and is retrying revocation with the provider.
authorization.identity: Account links remain. Provider authorization can be stopped or granted again without increasing community publishing limits.
